How do you get around the centralized nature of a discussion, and the feed page?

Usenet managed to get around this in the 1980s quite easily.

Essentially several centralized servers carry large portions of the discussion, possibly the whole thing. Individual users only access one centralized server at a time. The servers coordinate with one another over time to update the database. Writes to databases (which are changes) are far outweighed by reads in most database use cases, so costs between the nodes to update each other are small, and there's redundancy such that damage or destruction of one node does not actually disable the site in general.

To be fair, any reasonable web hosting cluster looks very similar to this. Several load-balanced servers face the users and serve HTTP requests from a cached database. Database writes and cache misses are forwarded back to the master database (Or DB cluster for fault tolerant or extra heavy duty workloads) for processing.

No central server = no central server costs... no bandwidth expenses. Just some public announcement website or some such.

Could save a massive bundle in the long run - like if VOAT hits 20 million users.
